solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sheep loudly escapes over the hill

indicators.note: whatever escapes is no longer there, so a letter goes missing from the word

blocks.note: a fold is a flock of sheep as well as their pen
f, forte, is the musical mark for loudly

explanation.surface: A noisy sheep breaks out of its field and bolts off over the hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over the hill' reads as the direction the sheep runs, but it is the definition. FOLD loses its F to leave OLD.
explanation.definitionFit: Over the hill is an idiom for someone past their prime, too aged to be useful.

clue.text: Youth discovered away from home

indicators.note: dis-covered means stripped of its cover, so the outside letters are peeled away

blocks.note: the word with its first and last letters removed

explanation.surface: A young runaway is found living away from home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' looks like 'found', but read as dis-covered it means uncovered: YOUTH without its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is out is not in, not at their house at the moment.

clue.text: Give up match after passes one’s squandered

indicators.note: something squandered is wasted and gone, so a letter is thrown away
coming after means placed behind, so the earlier-named piece is written second

blocks.note: to pass away is to die
the Roman numeral for one
a match is a pair, two things that go together

explanation.surface: A footballer gives up on the match after wasting pass after pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passes' sounds like football, but to pass away is to die; 'one's squandered' tells you that word loses its I.
explanation.definitionFit: To despair is to lose all hope, abandoning expectation that things will improve.

clue.text: Stones frontman finally produces music and scripts for a film

indicators.note: finally points to the very end, so only the closing letter is kept

blocks.note: scree is loose stones on a mountain slope
the final letter of this word
a musician who produces music plays

explanation.surface: Mick Jagger, the Rolling Stones' frontman, finally makes music and also writes film scripts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stones frontman' suggests Mick Jagger, but Stones is SCREE and only the last letter of frontman is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A screenplay is the written text of a movie, with dialogue and directions for the actors.

clue.text: Runners are on their feet about one thousand seconds after turning up

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a person, standing in for the noun

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning something up flips it so it reads from the bottom

blocks.note: re means about, concerning
the Roman numeral for one
k stands for a thousand
s is the abbreviation for seconds

explanation.surface: Athletes are back on their feet a thousand seconds after showing up for a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runners' suggests athletes, but skis are runners too. RE, I, K and S read upwards give SKIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A skier is a person with skis, long sliding runners, strapped to their boots.

clue.text: Dance music genre got confused with Afrobeats at first

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter is wanted
confused letters are muddled up into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: A dance music style became mixed up with Afrobeats in its early days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Music genre' looks like the definition, but genre is fodder; mix GENRE GOT with A.
explanation.definitionFit: Reggaeton is a Latin dance style from Puerto Rico, blending reggae and hip-hop rhythms.

clue.text: Result of late-opening venues — dancing

indicators.note: an opening that is late has gone, so the first letter is missing
dancing letters move about and change places

blocks.note: the word without its first letter

explanation.surface: Clubs that stay open late lead to people dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late-opening venues' reads as nightclubs, but late means former: VENUES loses its opening V.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to follow as a consequence, the verb sense of result.

clue.text: Quietly, he follows one with pear cider crossing border

indicators.note: what follows comes behind, so the earlier-named piece is written second
to cross something can mean to span it, so one piece stretches across the other

blocks.note: perry is cider made from pears
the Roman numeral for one
p, piano, is the musical mark for quietly
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man quietly walks behind someone carrying pear cider across a frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: Perry is cider made from pears, a drink of the English West Country; 'crossing' has it straddle the string built from the first half of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The periphery is the outer edge or boundary of an area.

clue.text: Group of states in area north of Crimea undergoing struggles

indicators.note: in a down entry, being north means sitting above, so one piece comes first
something struggling twists and writhes, so the letters are thrown about

blocks.note: a is the abbreviation for area
taken as written

explanation.surface: A news report on a bloc of countries in a war zone north of Crimea.
explanation.walkthrough: The geography is a decoy: 'north of' just puts A above the rearranged CRIMEA.
explanation.definitionFit: The United States of America is a federation of fifty states, so a group of states describes it.

clue.text: Sly maestro’s forged arrangement of The Planets

indicators.note: a forged thing is faked or hammered into new shape, so the letters are remade

blocks.note: taken as written, the possessive s included

explanation.surface: A crafty conductor faked his own arrangement of Holst's orchestral suite The Planets.
explanation.walkthrough: The Planets is Holst's famous suite, which makes 'arrangement' look musical; it is the definition read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Our solar system is the sun with the planets that orbit it, so the planets taken together name it.

clue.text: Difficult cricket match in the capital of Grenada

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its capital letter, the one at the front

blocks.note: a Test is an international cricket match
taken as written
the opening letter of the island's name

explanation.surface: A tough cricket match played in St George's, Grenada's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital of Grenada is St George's, but here capital means first letter, G.
explanation.definitionFit: Testing conditions are hard ones that stretch you, so the adjective means hard or demanding.

clue.text: Bizarre King Lear adaptation by American revolutionary

indicators.note: a revolution turns something right round, so the letters face the other way
an adaptation reworks its source, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: US is short for American
R, rex, is the abbreviation for king
taken as written

explanation.surface: A strange new version of King Lear staged by an American radical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American revolutionary' suggests a figure like Paul Revere, but it is the country's abbreviation turned round. 'King Lear' splits into two pieces: the Latin abbreviation for king and the name to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Surreal describes something dreamlike and odd, unreal in a way that unsettles.

clue.text: Steps song covered by Wicked cast’s back in vogue

indicators.note: something wicked is twisted, so its letters are bent into a new order
a thing covered by another is wrapped inside it
the back of a word is its end, so only the last letter is kept

blocks.note: taken as written, the possessive s included
an air is a tune or song
the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: A song by the pop group Steps, covered by the cast of the musical Wicked, is fashionable again.
explanation.walkthrough: Steps were a British pop group and Wicked is a stage musical, but Steps is the definition and Wicked the anagram signal for the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: A staircase is a flight of steps between floors, so steps describes it.

clue.text: One of two brothers who had each other’s back?

definitions.text: One of two brothers who had each other’s back?

blocks.clueFragment: One of two brothers who had each other’s back?
blocks.note: surface reading: a loyal brother, one of a pair who always supported each other
setter's reading: literally joined at the back, as conjoined twins can be

explanation.walkthrough: To have someone's back is an idiom for loyal support; read literally it describes brothers physically joined. The term comes from Chang and Eng Bunker, conjoined twins born in Siam.
explanation.definitionFit: Siamese twin is the older name for one of a pair of conjoined twins, born physically joined.

clue.text: Former convent’s east facade gotten rid of

indicators.note: what has been got rid of is removed, so a letter leaves the word

blocks.note: a priory is a religious house, which may be a convent of nuns
in an across entry east is the right-hand end, so its facade is the last letter

explanation.surface: The east front of an old convent has been demolished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Former convent' looks like a phrase, but 'Former' alone is the definition; PRIORY loses its final Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Prior means earlier or previous, as in a prior engagement, so it matches former.

clue.text: Cry of pain from Graham, upset after rear-end’s pinched

indicators.note: pinched means stolen, so the hindmost letter is taken away
upset things are knocked over and jumbled into a new order

blocks.note: the name without its last letter

explanation.surface: Graham yelps in distress after someone pinches his bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinched' suggests a painful nip, which fits the cry; it really means taken, removing GRAHAM's M.
explanation.definitionFit: Aargh is an exclamation people shout when hurt, frustrated or in sudden distress.

clue.text: Gym implements groundbreaking equipment that’s installed on the hoof

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing in for the noun

blocks.note: a vaulting horse is a piece of gym apparatus
a hoe is a garden tool for breaking up soil

explanation.surface: Innovative fitness gear that can be put in place on the move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groundbreaking' reads as innovative but is literal: a tool that breaks ground. 'On the hoof' reads as on the go but is literal too.
explanation.definitionFit: A horseshoe is a curved iron plate nailed to a horse's foot to protect it.

clue.text: One dumping rubbish by a railway in remote location

blocks.note: to tip rubbish is to dump it, so a tipper is someone who does
taken as written
RY is an abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Fly-tipping by a railway line out in the middle of nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Tipperary is an Irish county, made famous by the wartime song It's a Long Way to Tipperary.
explanation.definitionFit: The song's refrain says it is a long way to Tipperary, so the place is the byword for far away.

clue.text: Demonic gang on steamship starts to exhibit depravity

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters

blocks.note: a posse is a gang or band
SS is the prefix for a steamship
the opening letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A devilish gang aboard a ship begins to behave wickedly.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'on' puts one piece above another, so the gang is written before the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone possessed is controlled by an evil spirit, which is the sense of demonic here.

clue.text: English knight with black eye’s right to move treasures

indicators.note: one letter is told to move, changing the word's letter order

blocks.note: E is short for English
N is the knight in chess notation
a shiner is a black eye, plus the possessive s

explanation.surface: An English knight with a black eye has the right to shift valuables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' reads as an entitlement, but it is R: in SHINERS the R moves up three places.
explanation.definitionFit: To enshrine something is to cherish it and hold it sacred, so it means treasures as a verb.

clue.text: Flyer from on-street convenience store

indicators.note: in a down entry, one thing on another sits above it, so it comes first

blocks.note: Spar is a chain of small convenience shops, common in Britain and Europe
row is a word for a street of houses, as in Savile Row

explanation.surface: A leaflet picked up from the corner shop down the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flyer' suggests a leaflet, which suits the shop; it is a bird. Spar is a convenience-store chain.
explanation.definitionFit: A sparrow is a small brown bird, and any bird is something that flies.

clue.text: A number of Germans on the stern of my boat

indicators.note: the stern is the rear of a ship, so the last letter is wanted

blocks.note: the final letter of this word
acht is German for eight

explanation.surface: Several German tourists are standing at the back of my boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A number of Germans' looks like a group of people; it is a number in German. Across, 'on' lets ACHT follow Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A yacht is a sailing or motor vessel used for pleasure or racing.

clue.text: Establish two companies with new content

indicators.note: content is what a thing holds inside, so one piece is put within the other

blocks.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, and a firm is another word for one
n is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Setting up a pair of businesses with fresh material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' means what is inside: N sits between the two words for company.
explanation.definitionFit: To confirm something is to show it is true, settling or verifying it beyond doubt.

clue.text: Wipe under a settee’s lining

indicators.note: a lining runs inside something, so the letters are found within the words

blocks.note: the letters run across these words

explanation.surface: Cleaning beneath the sofa and its inner fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under' looks like a position word but supplies the opening letters of the run.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase something is to rub it out or delete it, removing all trace.

clue.text: Head of publishing used to get upset about writer’s twisted pen-name

indicators.note: the head of something is its top, so the first letter is kept
upset things are knocked over and jumbled
twisted round, the letters end up facing the other way

blocks.note: the opening letter of this word
taken as written
on can mean about, as in a talk on history
the writer is the setter, so writer's means my

explanation.surface: A publishing boss is annoyed by an author's convoluted pen-name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Used to' reads as a past habit, but used is fodder. In crosswords the writer is the setter, so writer's is MY.
explanation.definitionFit: A pseudonym is a false name an author writes under, the same thing as a pen-name.

clue.text: Under pressure, one agent returned material for a novel

definitions.note: this points to PAPER; the published grid has PIPER, which the wordplay with one as I builds

indicators.note: in a down entry, being under means sitting below, so the following piece comes after
something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters read backwards

blocks.note: p is the symbol for pressure
the Roman numeral for one
a rep, representative, is a sales agent

explanation.surface: A literary agent under deadline pressure sends back a manuscript.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under pressure' sounds like stress, but in a down entry it puts P on top. One taken as A would give PAPER, which the definition wants; the grid has PIPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A novel is printed on paper, so the material for a book is the stuff its pages are made of.

clue.text: Toy truck

blocks.note: first meaning: a child's word for a doll
second meaning: a low wheeled platform for moving heavy loads or a film camera

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one toy, a model truck, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a child's doll and a small wheeled trolley used to shift heavy things.

clue.text: Admire either end of woodworkers’ ball-and-socket joint

blocks.note: the first letter OR the last letter, spelt out with the word or between them
the hip is a ball-and-socket joint

explanation.surface: Carpenters admire a ball-and-socket joint, a fine piece of joinery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Either end' is read literally as 'W or S', the first or last letter of woodworkers'. 'Joint' suggests carpentry; it is anatomy.
explanation.definitionFit: To worship someone is to adore and revere them, a stronger form of admiring.

clue.text: Will I be quiet or greedy?

blocks.note: Will Self is an English novelist
taken as written
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to stay silent or to be grasping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like the future tense; it is the first name of the writer Will Self, standing for his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Selfish people put themselves first and want more than their share, like greedy ones.

clue.text: Old Hebrew discarding a bra that could never be kosher

indicators.note: what is discarded is thrown out, so letters are dropped

blocks.note: Abraham is the Hebrew patriarch of Genesis
taken as written

explanation.surface: An elderly Jewish man throws away an unsuitable bra.
explanation.walkthrough: The bra seems a joke garment, but it is literal letters: ABRAHAM without A BRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ham is pork, and pork is forbidden under Jewish dietary law, so it can never be kosher.

clue.text: Crossword setter’s ready, say, for a bank holiday

blocks.note: a setter's anagram signal: in reverse, the word a compiler would place before letters to be rearranged
taken as written, the letters a setter would ask you to rearrange

explanation.surface: A puzzle compiler says they are all set for the bank holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as if it were a clue. Its first word is a typical anagram signal, and the rest rearranged spells 'ready, say', so it is a crossword setter's way of writing those words.
explanation.definitionFit: The first of January is a public holiday in Britain, where bank holidays are official days off.

clue.text: Silence out of which you first emerged

definitions.text: out of which you first emerged

blocks.note: first meaning: keeping quiet

blocks.clueFragment: out of which you first emerged
blocks.note: second meaning: a mother, who gave birth to you

explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads like a description of silence breaking, but it describes a parent. Mum is the British word for mom.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping mum means saying nothing, and your mum is the mother who bore you.
